teaser.text: Linde plc sells gases that other businesses and hospitals cannot afford to make or deliver unreliably. It earns that revenue by owning production plants, running delivery networks, and sometimes building the plants themselves, so every dollar of sales must also fund energy, people, maintenance and long-lived equipment.

stock.opening: Linde's probability-weighted price is $606.80 in October 2029, with a 29% total return including dividends. It hinges on profitable project starts, cash generation and the valuation multiple holding up.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Linde's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Linde's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is $527.34 in October 2027, representing a 10% total return including dividends. It reaches $564.32 in October 2028, or 18%, and $606.80 in October 2029, or 29%. The 2029 range runs from $419.67 in the bear case to $800.61 in the bull case. The reference price is $487.35.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Linde?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires uneven industrial demand, delayed projects and weaker margins to reduce EBITDA and cash conversion.

The bull case requires semiconductor and industrial demand to strengthen, projects to ramp on schedule and cash generation to support both investment and buybacks. It reaches $590.58 initially and $800.61 by October 2029. Its probability is 20% because backlog is an opportunity, not yet realized earnings.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Linde really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operating cash flow was $10,350 million and capital spending was $5,261 million. That left $5,089 million of free cash flow before the owner-oriented deduction for $164 million of stock compensation. Base capex was $2,618 million, while project capex was $2,643 million. Base spending includes some growth, so it is not pure maintenance.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Linde today?

paragraphs.text: At **$487.35 on October 13, 2026**, Linde’s shares were worth **$224,658.68 million** in total. Enterprise value was **$247,773.68 million** because it adds debt and subtracts cash. Market value measures only shareholders’ claim; enterprise value treats the business as if a buyer paid shareholders, took on its debt and kept its cash. Linde’s lenders therefore have a claim on future plant cash before shareholders do.

blocks.heading: How much does Linde pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $6.36 per share to $7.14 in the base case, using 6% annual increases below the historical 9.1% growth rate. The bear freezes at $6.36 because payouts already exceeded free cash flow, while the bull reaches $7.70 as earnings and project cash generation improve.

blocks.heading: Is Linde's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Linde funded substantial investment, but it also paid shareholders more than the cash remaining after that investment in every year from 2021 through 2025.

In 2025, operating cash flow was $10,350 million and capital spending was $5,261 million. That left $5,089 million of free cash flow before the owner-oriented deduction for $164 million of stock compensation. Base capex was $2,618 million, while project capex was $2,643 million. Base spending includes some growth, so it is not pure maintenance.

paragraphs.text: The forecast would move toward the bear case if manufacturing demand weakens during 2027–2028, especially where lower delivered-gas utilization pressures margins. A delayed Phoenix ramp or other project start during 2027–2029 would reduce growth and free cash flow, causing Linde to retain cash and trim buybacks.

earnings.meta_description: Linde reports on October 29, 2026; guidance calls for higher earnings with more spending, while project startups, cash conversion and Lincare matter.
earnings.opening: Linde reports its next results on October 29, 2026. Watch project startups and cash conversion, especially Lincare's margin pressure.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Linde's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Linde guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Capital expenditure, or capex, buys long-lived assets such as gas-production machinery, pipes and infrastructure. Management raised the planned spending range while slightly lifting the earnings floor. That means Linde is committing more cash before the related plants produce their full returns.

blocks.heading: Did Linde keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The practical test is the resulting share count and per-share earnings, not the announcement of a buyback. Management also met its 2025 adjusted earnings-per-share forecast, although adjusted figures exclude selected items. More recently, after-tax return on capital was 23.5% in the second quarter of 2026, down from 25.1% a year earlier.

blocks.heading: What do Linde's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was $9,289 million, up 9.3% from a year earlier. The underlying increase was 4.0%, divided between price and volume. Almost half of the volume increase came from new project startups, so the quarter was only partly a recovery in existing customer demand.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Linde's next results?

paragraphs.text: Linde reports Q3 results on October 29, 2026, with the call at 9 a.m. Eastern time. Investors should look for project startups and cash conversion, but also for Lincare, the U.S. homecare business that management identified as the main source of Americas margin pressure. Management is examining its strategic fit, though an evaluation is not a promise to sell.
